query: An equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy has a simple solid-solution structure and favorable plasticity and machinability but relatively low hardness and strength, while its microstructure and deformation behavior remain insufficiently understood. Under hardness testing and mechanical loading of this starting state, what single intervention could overcome the strength and hardness limitation while retaining its favorable mechanical characteristics? State the proposed intervention, its mechanism, the predicted measurable change relative to the unmodified alloy, its applicable processing and test conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a microstructural and mechanical experiment that could falsify the hypothesis.

falsification_experiment.design: prepare CoCrFeNiTi alloys with varying Ti content and test their mechanical properties
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: if the addition of Ti does not improve the strength and hardness of the CoCrFeNi alloy, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: High entropy alloys (HEAs) are composed of five or more elements at equal or nearly equal atomic ratios [,,,] HEAs tend to form a stable solid solution phase and have excellent mechanical properties and corrosion resistance, unlike the traditional alloys that are typically based on one or two principal elements. Therefore, HEAs have been heavily researched and attracted much attention from the academic community [,,]. The CoCrFeNi HEA system has become important, because of its excellent corrosion resistance, ductility, and thermal stability [,]. Surface engineering technologies, such as laser cladding and plasma spraying, can reduce the cost and increase the value of the HEAs for industrial applications []. However, the CoCrFeNi HEA system cannot meet the needs of high-strength parts due to its poor mechanical strength. It has been demonstrated that a hard secondary phase can be formed in the CoCrFeNi matrix by adding a small amount of Nb, Ti, or Mo, resulting in precipitation strengthening and improvement of the mechanical properties []. The CoCrFeNi system is one of the most important high entropy alloys (HEAs) systems. By adding and adjusting the alloy element components and using different synthesis methods, different phases, organization and microstructure can be obtained, thus improving their properties. In this study, CoCrFeNiTix HEAs with various Ti contents (x in molar ratio, x = 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5) were fabricated by an electrochemical process by virtue of different oxides. The impacts of different Ti contents on the structure, distribution of elements, mechanical properties and corrosion behavior were researched using XRD, EDX and other testing methods. The bulk CoCrFeNiTix (x = 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5) HEAs could be obtained through vacuum hot pressing sintering process (VHPS), which had a single-phase FCC structure.
